observations.explanation: The paper describes 2,294 tasks drawn from real GitHub issues and merged PRs, filtered for issue resolution, test changes, and fail-to-pass test behavior (pp. 1–3, 15, 18–19). That supports the claim of realistic, useful-scale benchmark construction.

The paper reports low resolution rates, including Claude 2’s 4.8% with oracle retrieval (pp. 5–6). Oracle retrieval provides files edited by the reference patch, while the authors note it is less realistic and may omit needed context (p. 4).

The authors state that all benchmark instances are Python and that execution-based testing alone cannot guarantee reliable performance or capture qualities such as comprehensiveness, efficiency, and readability (p. 9).

This is carefully framed as an uncertainty about the inspected pages, not a claim that the paper lacks details. The paper supplies additional prompting and inference information in the appendices, including a prompt template and greedy-decoding setup (pp. 24–25); it also says prompt variations generally did not substantially affect performance, with stated exceptions (p. 25).
